messages:
marta: Heads up: running the quarterly entitlement sampler and found a service account with org-level Owner role still granted via a legacy group (analytics-ops@redwood.org). This SA is tied to an old ETL job `analytics-backfill-v2`. anyone familiar? :grimacing:

jonah: whoa. owner at org-level is definitely not expected. can you paste the binding?

marta: snippet from iam export: `{\"role\":\"roles/owner\",\"members\":[\"serviceAccount:etl-backfill-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com\"]}`. It was granted through group-membership: `group:analytics-ops@redwood.org`.

kevin: that SA also has KMS decrypt on key `redwood-logs-ingest`. I see decrypts from batch nodes in the audit logs as far back as 2025-08. we should treat this as an entitlement escalation candidate.

tania: product note: the backfill runs infrequently but when it runs it touches large historical datasets. revoking perms without a plan could break late-arriving telemetry processing. we need a staged approach.

marta: proposal: 1) snapshot current IAM policies + export recent audit logs, 2) create a scoped role with only needed permissions (storage read, kms.decrypt limited to specific key ring), 3) deploy the scoped role to a canary project and switch one backfill job, 4) observe for two runs, 5) remove org-level owner binding and enforce least-priv via automation.

jonah: agree. step 0: record exact bindings. commands: `gcloud organizations get-iam-policy ORG_ID --format=json > /tmp/org-iam-2635004321.json` and `gsutil cp /tmp/org-iam-2635004321.json gs://redwood-audit/iam-snapshots/2635004321.json`

kevin: note on logs: our KMS audit retention for that project is only 30 days. we should pull a 6-month slice before we change anything, for vulnerability triage and compliance. I'll start the export job: `gcloud logging read \"resource.type=kms_key\" --project=redwood-prod --start-time=\"2025-09-01T00:00:00Z\" --end-time=\"2026-03-20T00:00:00Z\" --format=json > /tmp/kms-audit.json`

marta: opening a low-impact incident to track this as an entitlement cleanup (INC-2026-053). tagging @compliance. sre-bot: create ticket please.

sre-bot: created INC-2026-053, severity: P3, owners: @marta @kevin. Link: https://inc.internal/INC-2026-053

tania: on rollback risk: can we wrap the switch in a feature-flag-like flow? e.g., use an environment variable KEY_ID that the job reads, and update that in k8s via a rolling restart for a single replica first.

jonah: yep. we can add a runtime toggle. Also recommend adding a pre-deploy lint: fail if any new grants use `roles/owner` or `roles/editor` at org/folder scope. simple check: `if policy_binding.role in [\"roles/owner\",\"roles/editor\"] and binding.scope in [\"organization\",\"folder\"]: fail`

kevin: for long-term: add an automated least-privilege scanner that runs monthly, creates PRs with suggested scoped roles, and opens incidents for any owner-level principals tied to service accounts. we can use an internal GH action to create the PRs.

marta: compliance question: does anyone know if that analytics group membership is managed in SCIM? if it came from the partner onboarding pipeline we may need legal notified. compliance-bot, can you check group provenance?

compliance-bot: group analytics-ops@redwood.org created 2019-11-04. Provisioning source: identity-provider (SCIM). Suggested action: verify owners and org-admin approvals before removal.

tania: good catch. we'll coordinate with identity team for owner attestations. timeline: start canary switch tomorrow 02:00 UTC, observe two runs, then remove org-owner grant 24hrs after canary success.

kevin: I'll also add a temporary alert rule: any use of org-level owner by a workload (non-interactive principal) sends a pager to sec-oncall. rule example: `logMatch: protoPayload.methodName=\"SetIamPolicy\" AND resource.name: \"organizations/ORG_ID\" AND protoPayload.authorizationInfo.permission:\"resourcemanager.organizations.setIamPolicy\"`

jonah: for the vulnerability triage doc, please capture how the binding appeared (manual grant vs automation). also capture whether any stale service account keys exist. run: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=etl-backfill-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-prod`

marta: I'm running the key list now. if keys exist older than 90 days we'll rotate and disable. also attaching a quick post-action checklist: - snapshot IAM + logs, - canary scoped role, - run-backfill on canary, - rotate SA keys, - remove org owner binding, - add monthly scanner + GH PR automation, - update runbook.

kevin: we should also update KMS key policy to deny org-level bindings by default. guardrail idea: OPA/Gatekeeper policy that denies KMS role bindings to groups unless explicitly allowlisted.

tania: +1. after canary success, let's file a short blameless note summarizing root cause and remediation steps and share with eng leads. compliance needs the evidence bundle for Q audit.

marta: logged artifacts to the incident bucket: gs://redwood-audit/entitlement-incidents/INC-2026-053/iam-snapshot.json and kms-audit-6mo.json. I'll post progress updates here during the canary tomorrow. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
